title: Split customers.full_name into first_name and last_name
task: Finance needs first and last name as separate fields on customers for the new invoicing template.

must_identify: Dropping full_name in the same migration that runs BEFORE the rolling deploy breaks the old app version for ~4 minutes (old code still INSERTs/SELECTs full_name) and makes rollback of the app impossible without a data-restoring migration; needs expand-migrate-contract across at least two releases

The DROP COLUMN is irreversible for the original string: the down migration can only reconstruct an approximation, and names like 'Mary Ann Smith', single names and company names are split lossy by split_part on the first space; original data is lost

The single UPDATE over 2.1M rows and NOT NULL DEFAULT '' additions take locks on a live table; the runbook documents an 11-minute lock incident for ADD COLUMN DEFAULT; backfill should be batched (or at least acknowledged as an operational event)
API breaking change: POST /customers no longer accepts full_name; callers must be migrated or the API must accept both for a period
nice_to_have: Keep full_name (or a generated/display column) and add first/last as nullable; backfill in batches; switch readers; drop later with a separate approved migration
Decide the split rule for multi-word names explicitly and with Finance
PITR window is 7 days; plan has no backup verification step before a destructive migration
should_not: Treat the migration as routine because the diff is small
Focus on code style while missing the data-loss problem
human_decisions: Accept lossy heuristic split vs manual/assisted split for ambiguous names
API compatibility window for full_name callers
Whether full_name should be dropped at all
fixture_facts: customers table has full_name TEXT NOT NULL (0002_customers.sql); 2.1M rows per runbook
docs/ops-runbook.txt: migrations run before rolling deploy; old and new versions overlap ~4 minutes; ADD COLUMN DEFAULT lock incident; PITR 7 days
